newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs becalmed before threat of stormy July.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs becalmed before threat of stormy July.

text.p: Belgian OLOs moved erratically but in a tight range on Thursday with many investors already looking toward a potentially stormy July, dealers said.

The benchmark 10-year yield BE286= oscillated between 5.77 and 5.74 percent compared with 5.76 percent at Wednesday's close, while the spread over similar Bunds MEUR widened slightly to nine from eight basis points.

Dealers said the reason for the underperformance was probably the approach of the Treasury's monthly OLO auction on Monday BELA where the benchmark five- and 10-year bonds will be on offer, but other factors also loomed.

"Some people are already looking ahead to next week's FOMC meeting," one trader said, referring to the U.S. Fed's policy-making committee due to meet on July 1 and 2. analysts believed the Fed would raise rates at that meeting. But an American Bankers Association panel said separately the Fed should hike rates by 25 basis points "this summer".
The ABA panel expected U.S. growth to rebound in the second half of the year from around two percent in the second quarter. Final first quarter GDP data are due on Friday US-ECI.
Most players are looking to the U.S. non-farm payrolls report due next Friday to provide clues on U.S. interest rates.

Further out, attention was likely to switch to Europe and worries over monetary union, dealers said. The German government, lagging in its bid to meet the Maastricht criteria, is due to approve its 1998 budget and adjustments to its 1997 budget on July 11. Before that the opposition Social Democrats are threatening to reject a tax reform package.
France's Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn reiterated on Thursday its public finances were also in a serious state.
